title: Image pinset correlator and dependency-graph sweeper for staged rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Scope: Build an "Image Pinset Correlator" service and an associated "Dependency Graph Sweeper" job that together enable deterministic, cohort-based staged rollouts for container images across driver/CUDA matrices. The feature should ingest SBOMs and image manifests, correlate layer provenance and package dependencies, and produce a versioned pinset that pairs container images with validated driver stacks and kernel constraints.

Goals:
- Automatically compute a compatibility score for candidate images against known CUDA/driver combinations using SBOM layer analysis and historical rollout telemetry.
- Generate cohort groups (pinsets) for canary, ramp, and full rollout gates with explicit rollback targets.
- Surface incompatibilities (missing kernel modules, GPU driver ABI mismatches, required libc/toolchain versions) as actionable items in the Console rollouts page and in release metadata.
- Provide a sweep job that continuously reconciles deployed cohorts with upstream SBOM changes and flags images that require revalidation or rotation.

Design notes and constraints:
- Input sources: container registry manifests (OCI), SBOM artifacts (CycloneDX/ SPDX), internal artifact index, image attestation metadata.
- Correlator outputs a machine-readable pinset (sha256 image, sbom-id, driver-compat-list, min-kernel-version, risk-score). Pinset format must be backward-compatible with existing rollout API.
- Sweeper runs nightly and on publish events; it must be rate-limited and idempotent.
- The risk scoring model initially uses rule-based heuristics (layer provenance freshness, known CVEs from SBOM, ABI signature mismatch) and later will accept ML-derived signals from telemetry.
- Rollout integration: expose pinsets through the Console API so release engineers can select cohorts and enable automated fallback to a validated fallback pinset on error budget burn.

Acceptance criteria:
- Service can ingest SBOMs for 95% of images we currently ship and produce a validated pinset within 3 minutes per image on average.
- Console displays compatibility score and top 3 incompatibility causes for any image.
- Sweeper produces daily reconciliation report; any image with risk-score >= 0.7 must have an assigned follow-up task or be auto-quarantined depending on policy.
- End-to-end canary rollout with a pinset must be testable in staging and support automated rollback to previous pinset on latency or error SLO breach.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives from SBOM parsing: include manual override for pinset generation and add sampling of images for human review.
- Scale: index and sharding strategy for correlator metadata; initial pilot limited to runtime LTS channels.
- Security: SBOM ingestion requires signed attestations; ensure KMS-backed verification and audit logging for every pinset change.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype SBOM parser and simple compatibility heuristic (2 sprints).
2) Implement correlator service API and pinset format, wire to artifact index (1 sprint).
3) Build sweeper job, nightly reconciliation reports, and quarantining policy (1 sprint).
4) Console integration: UI fields for compatibility score, incompatibility reasons, and rollout pinset selection (2 sprints).
5) Pilot on dedicated LTS channel images, iterate on heuristics based on pilot feedback (2 sprints).

Observability and metrics:
- Pinset generation latency, ingestion success rate, average risk score per channel.
- Number of quarantined images and time-to-remediate.
- Rollout failure rate attributable to image/driver incompatibility.

Related artifacts and links:
- Design sketch: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/ABC123 (internal design doc)
- Prototype SBOM parser repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sbom-tools/pull/88
- Console mockups in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/rollouts-ui

Notes for reviewers: prioritise compatibility format stability and audit trail requirements. This work is a prerequisite for safer LTS rollouts and will reduce manual driver troubleshooting during enterprise upgrades.
